content_voiceover: Hepcidin is the master iron regulator, and this slide shows how the liver senses iron status to control it. Two membrane complexes act as iron sensors: HFE paired with transferrin receptor 2, and hemojuvelin paired with the BMP receptor. When iron is plentiful, these complexes signal through phosphorylated SMAD proteins into the nucleus, turning on hepcidin transcription. Hepcidin then goes up, which blocks ferroportin and drives iron down. Now add TMPRSS6, also called matriptase-2. Its job is to cleave hemojuvelin off the membrane. When TMPRSS6 is active, it shuts down the HJV-BMP signal, hepcidin falls, and iron rises to meet demand. This single pathway explains two important genetic diseases. First, if TMPRSS6 itself is mutated, it can't cleave hemojuvelin, so BMP signaling stays on, hepcidin stays inappropriately high, and the patient develops iron-refractory iron deficiency anemia, or IRIDA, which does not respond to oral iron. Second, if HFE, TfR2, or HJV are mutated, the sensing complex fails, the liver can't turn on hepcidin appropriately, hepcidin stays low despite iron overload, and the patient develops hereditary hemochromatosis. Knowing this pathway lets you predict the genotype from the phenotype and vice versa, which is exactly how these questions get tested.
keypoints: Iron sensor complex (HFE-TfR2, HJV-BMP) → SMAD → hepcidin ↑ → iron ↓
TMPRSS6 cleaves HJV → BMP signaling ↓ → hepcidin ↓ → iron ↑
TMPRSS6 mutation → IRIDA: high hepcidin, refractory to oral iron
HFE / TfR2 / HJV mutation → low hepcidin → hereditary hemochromatosis
keypoint_voiceover: Remember this as one pathway with two failure modes. Normally the iron sensor complex, HFE-TfR2 and HJV-BMP, signals through SMAD to raise hepcidin and lower iron. TMPRSS6 opposes this by cleaving hemojuvelin, which lowers hepcidin and raises iron. If TMPRSS6 is mutated, hepcidin stays high and iron can't be absorbed, causing IRIDA. If the sensor genes themselves, HFE, TfR2, or HJV, are mutated, hepcidin stays inappropriately low, causing hereditary hemochromatosis.
